title: Verification enforcement gates
description: Blocks ship while the phase's own verification artifacts still say the work is unproven. Core GSD produces VERIFICATION.md and VALIDATION.md but no gate reads either — a phase with gaps_found reaches ship unopposed.

workflow.verify_enforce.description: Block ship when VERIFICATION.md reports unproven truths (truths_unproven != 0). Requires the verifier to emit that field.

workflow.nyquist_enforce.description: Block ship when VALIDATION.md reports nyquist_compliant: false, or when the phase produced no VALIDATION.md at all.

workflow.mn_security_enforce.description: Block ship on open threats in SECURITY.md (threats_open must be 0). Unlike core workflow.security_enforcement, which blocks when the phase wrote no SECURITY.md, this gate declares the artifact optional: a phase with no SECURITY.md passes — absence of threats is not a defect. A SECURITY.md that exists is always read.

workflow.mn_windows_enforce.description: Block ship on open broken windows in WINDOWS.md (open_count must be 0). Unlike core workflow.windows_enforce, the artifact is optional: a phase with no WINDOWS.md passes. A WINDOWS.md that exists is always read.

workflow.assertion_ratchet.description: Block verification when the count of live assertions dropped or tests were newly skipped since the recorded baseline. Catches the one failure mode a green suite cannot report: a check that was deleted rather than fixed. The gate only reads: it needs .planning/assertion-baseline.json — create it, and re-record it after a deliberate drop, with `gsd_run mn assertion-baseline`; without one it blocks as unresolvable.

workflow.data_contract_for_ui.description: Instruct the planner to derive a field table from the Zod schema for any screen bound to a DTO, and to state the control, order, error copy and conditional-visibility decisions the schema cannot express. UI-SPEC.md carries no fields, so without this the designer invents them.

workflow.design_phase.description: Instruct the planner to fix layer placement and cross-plan signatures in {phase}-DESIGN.md before splitting the phase into plans. The split into plans IS the boundary decision, and nothing downstream records that it was made: PATTERNS.md answers what an existing file should be copied from, using a controller/service/model role vocabulary that cannot express layers like ports or rules. The concrete failure is signature divergence between parallel waves — wave 2's plan is written before wave 1's code exists, so it calls Promise<Book|null> against an EitherAsync port. Both plans verify green (files_modified disjoint, key_links matched, per-project tests pass) and the mismatch lands on the pre-commit typecheck with both commits already in history. Requires templates/DESIGN.md.

workflow.design_registry.description: Instruct the planner to read the project's DESIGN-SYSTEM.md and derive a node-to-code registry before any screen is planned. The bridge document already exists under the quality-design skill — component ids, states, zone map, screen registry — and nothing in the pipeline reads it: UI-SPEC.md carries palette and spacing but not one component, so the planner invents the component list. Derived half (does a file exist for this node) comes from `gsd_run mn design-registry`; the authored half (todo/done, deliberate divergence, breakpoints) stays in DESIGN-SYSTEM.md, which is authoritative only while it matches the live design file.

workflow.user_route.description: Instruct the planner to name the screens of a multi-screen phase and the route through them — inventory, stateDiagram-v2, and where every failure branch lands — before any screen is designed. Nothing upstream carries this: UI-SPEC.md mentions a page only as a spacing token, and the user story is one sentence naming an outcome, not a path.

workflow.spec_phase.description: Run spec-phase at the start of an autonomous phase, before discuss. Core reaches spec-phase from no route in autonomous.md or next.md, so SPEC.md is written only if someone types the command — and every consumer that reads it silently gets nothing. Non-blocking: a phase adequately specified by its roadmap entry continues to discuss without one.

workflow.migration_safety.description: Block the wave when a new .sql migration performs an operation that is irreversible without data loss (DROP COLUMN/TABLE, incompatible ALTER TYPE, NOT NULL without DEFAULT, TRUNCATE) and nobody declared it, or when meta/_journal.json disagrees with the .sql files on disk. schema-gate proves the schema was pushed and drift proves schema matches tree — a column-dropping migration passes both, because schema and code are consistent precisely because the column is gone. Also instructs the planner to settle backfill, ordering and the undo path before the migration is written. Silenced per-file by `-- gsd:irreversible`, `-- gsd:backfill`, `-- gsd:reverse:`, `-- gsd:manual`, or by a phase artifact that discusses rollback/backfill.

workflow.migration_safety_strict.description: Tighten workflow.migration_safety: warnings (USING casts, duplicate migration indices) also block, and a destructive statement must be declared in the .sql itself — prose in PLAN.md no longer silences it. Off by default because the looser form already forces the decision; turn on for domains where a bad migration is unrecoverable.

workflow.blast_radius.description: Block verification when files changed by the phase were named by no PLAN.md in it. files_modified is a declaration nothing checks after the fact — ADR-1239 specifies the check and neither isolation adapter implements it (#2596). Divergence is the signal, not volume: a phase legitimately touching 105 files is fine, one touching a file nobody planned is not.

workflow.verify_gates.description: Object of check name → command line, run by `gsd_run verify gates` and recorded into {phase}-VERIFICATION.md's frontmatter under `gates:`. Set it with `gsd_run query config-set workflow.verify_gates '{"tests":"npm test","typecheck":"npx tsc --noEmit","lint":"npm run lint"}'` or write the object into config.json directly. Empty (the default) means the command refuses rather than recording a green field that proves nothing — only the project knows what its own green looks like. Written by a command so the numbers a verifier is judged on do not come from the agent being judged; the exit code of a typecheck cannot be optimistic. A value that is set but cannot run (an empty or non-string command, or a legacy JSON-text string that does not parse to such an object) makes `verify gates` fail with reason invalid_checks_config naming each problem, never with no_checks_configured. Each check is recorded with a status from a closed set — pass, fail, stale (the command could not run as a check: exit 127/126, a spawn error, a signal or the output cap), timeout — so a roster that outlived its tools is reported as stale with a warning, never as a red check and never as a green one.

workflow.verify_gates_record.description: Run `verify gates` automatically at verify:pre, before the verifier reads the phase. Order matters: the verifier should read numbers it did not produce. Off by default because it is inert without workflow.verify_gates naming commands, and running an unconfigured recorder on every phase would print a refusal each time.

workflow.verify_gates_baseline.description: Measure the project's checks (workflow.verify_gates) at execute:pre, before the first wave, into {phase}-BASELINE.md (`gsd_run verify baseline`), and block the run while the base is red (`gsd_run check mn-baseline`). A phase that starts on a red tree finishes on one, and nothing then tells the failures it inherited from the ones it introduced. A check that cannot run (stale command, timeout) blocks as unmeasured, not as red. To start on a known red base, record why: `gsd_run verify baseline --phase N --accept "<reason>"` — the gate passes while every non-green check is on that list, and a check that goes red later still blocks. The record carries a digest of the working tree outside .planning/ and of the roster, so a record of other code is never read as this one. Off by default: it blocks, and it costs one full run of the checks per execute-phase; turned on silently it would halt every existing project whose roster has a known red check.

workflow.tool_preflight.description: Halt execute-phase at execute:pre when a plan still to run names a tool its executor's installed agent does not grant — an mcp__<server>__… name, a .pen design file (Pencil MCP), or WebFetch/WebSearch/NotebookEdit/AskUserQuestion (`gsd_run check mn-tool-preflight`). The message names the plan, the missing grants and the fix: `gsd-tools config-set agent_tools.<agent> '[…]'` and a reinstall (agent_tools, #4032), or a first-party capability's agentTools (ADR-5210). Without it the orchestrator met such a plan by running general-purpose in place of gsd-executor, outside the executor's contract. The grants are read from the installed agent file the runtime loads; when that file cannot be read the gate passes and says so. On by default (absent = enabled): it blocks only a plan that cannot be executed as written.

workflow.verify_gates_enforce.description: Block ship unless every check in the recorded `gates:` block passed (`gsd_run check mn-verify-gates`). workflow.verify_enforce reads truths_unproven, which the verifier writes about itself; this reads what the commands returned. A red check is a finding naming each check and its exit code; a check recorded as stale (its command not found or not executable, exit 127/126, or cut off by the environment) or timed out is reported as not measured — it still blocks, because a check that could not run proves nothing, but the message sends you to the roster rather than calling the code broken. Requires workflow.verify_gates_record (or a manual `verify gates` run) to have recorded anything — a phase with no `gates:` block fails this gate rather than passing it, because an absent measurement is not a green one.

workflow.mutation_spot_check.description: Block verification when a mutant survives in code the phase declared: the source is changed in one place (>= to >, === to !==, true to false), the project's own test command runs, and a suite that stays green proves nothing checks that behaviour. workflow.assertion_ratchet catches a check that was DELETED; it cannot catch one that never checked anything, since expect(true).toBe(true) counts the same as a real assertion. This project has the case on record — a summary reading "my own test was a false green, caught by mutation" — found by hand, and left as a technique someone has to remember rather than a step that runs. Runs as a verify:pre step (`gsd_run verify mutation`, bounded to nine minutes) that records a mutation: block in VERIFICATION.md; the gate reads that record and blocks on a survivor, on a missing or stale record, or when the step could not check. Requires workflow.mutation_test_command. Refuses (rather than reporting kills) on an already-red suite, where a killed mutant cannot be told from a pre-existing failure.

workflow.mutation_test_command.description: Test command the mutation spot-check runs, e.g. "npx vitest run --project unit" or "npx nx affected -t test". Uses the project's own runner rather than a mutation framework: neither mn nor awesome-projects installs Stryker, and a gate that first requires installing a tool does not get switched on. Prefer the narrowest command that still covers the phase — the check runs it once per mutant.

workflow.mutation_max_mutants.description: How many mutants the spot-check introduces per phase (one per declared source file). It is a spot-check, not coverage: killing three says the tests react at three points, which is the claim being made. Each mutant costs one full run of workflow.mutation_test_command, and the step stops starting new ones once its nine-minute budget is spent.

workflow.worktree_provision.description: Equip each new worktree at creation instead of letting an agent discover it is unequipped by failing. Copies .mcp.json and .claude/settings*.json (the recorded failure: mcp__pencil__* and atlas unavailable in every worktree agent, because the config lives in the main checkout), provides node_modules per workflow.worktree_deps, and refuses a worktree whose base is further behind the main checkout than workflow.worktree_max_base_lag. Off by default because it copies files and may run an install command. Implemented by hooks/gsd-worktree-provision.js, which the installer registers on Claude Code's WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove: that hook replaces the harness's own creation whether or not this key is on — it creates <main checkout>/.claude/worktrees/<name> on branch worktree-<name> from the local HEAD (never a stale origin/HEAD) and copies .worktreeinclude files; `--worktree "#N"` (which Claude Code turns into the name pr-N) is based on that pull/merge request's head fetched from origin instead. Equipment runs only in a GSD project — a .planning/config.json inside the repository; any other git project gets just the worktree and the .worktreeinclude copy, so "absent key = enabled" never reaches a project without .planning/. A failed equipment step warns unless workflow.worktree_provision_strict is on; the warnings are recorded in the worktree's git dir and handed to the agent in the first session started there. Runtimes without that event keep their existing dispatch path.

workflow.worktree_provision_strict.description: Refuse the worktree when an equipment step fails (a tool-config or .worktreeinclude copy, the node_modules link, the install command) instead of warning (a warning reaches the agent in the worktree's first session). The half-equipped worktree and its branch are removed again before the hook exits non-zero, so a creation Claude Code reports as failed leaves nothing on disk (a rollback that cannot finish says what it left behind). Off by default: an agent that may not need the missing piece is better served by a worktree than by none, and refusing isolation over an optional convenience is how people come to turn it off. Only consulted when workflow.worktree_provision is on, in a GSD project.

workflow.worktree_deps.description: How a provisioned worktree gets its dependencies. "link" symlinks the main checkout's node_modules — fast, and correct whenever the lockfile has not moved, which is the common case for a phase branch. "install" runs workflow.worktree_install_command for the cases where it has. "none" leaves it alone. A failure here warns rather than refusing the worktree (the phase may not need dependencies, and blocking isolation over an optional convenience is how people come to distrust it) unless workflow.worktree_provision_strict is on.

workflow.worktree_install_command.description: Command run inside a new worktree when workflow.worktree_deps is "install" (e.g. "bun install --frozen-lockfile"). Empty means the install step reports that nothing was configured rather than guessing a package manager.

workflow.worktree_max_base_lag.description: Refuse a worktree whose base is more than this many commits behind the main checkout (0 disables the check). Plans written against a stale base are written against code that has already moved — recorded in the ucars retrospective as "worktree 380 commits behind main at start", discovered mid-phase. This is the one provisioning step that BLOCKS, because unlike a missing tool it cannot be worked around: the work has to be redone. An unmeasurable base (shallow clone, unrelated histories) warns instead — refusing there would strand the phase, and the executor's own first build surfaces it anyway.

workflow.worktree_copy_tools.description: Copy .mcp.json and .claude/settings*.json into a provisioned worktree so an agent has the tools it had a moment ago. An existing file in the worktree is never clobbered — a worktree carrying its own settings is making a deliberate statement. Only consulted when workflow.worktree_provision is on.

workflow.autonomous_max_phases.description: Stop an autonomous run after this many phases (0 = no limit, the prior behaviour). Overridable per run with --max-phases N. The run ends by choosing to, at a phase boundary where work is committed and verified — which is reviewable — rather than by exhausting its context mid-phase, which is not. Long-run failure in agentic coding is measured to be dominated by exhaustion (MAX_TURNS, wall clock), not by a wrong decision at the end; a harness that stops cleanly costs far less per unit of work delivered than one that runs until it cannot.

workflow.uat_enforce.description: Block ship while the phase's own {phase}-UAT.md still lists manual checks nobody ran. The verifier already writes them there when it cannot confirm a truth by reading code, and `audit-uat` already finds them — nothing read that, so a phase whose report says "nobody checked" shipped anyway. A phase with no UAT file passes (most defer nothing); a FAILED item passes too, because a failed manual check is a known defect that verification owns, and this gate asks only whether anything went unrun.

workflow.clean_state_enforce.description: Block ship while the working tree has changes outside .planning/ or git is halfway through a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert. ship.md already asks the model to read `git status --short` and stop; this makes it an exit code, and adds the one state status cannot show: a stopped rebase or cherry-pick leaves the tree clean while history is mid-operation. Changes under .planning/ are ignored (they move while the work runs), and a leftover .continue-here.md is not counted (resume does not delete it, so it does not mean the session was dropped).

workflow.prohibition_guard.description: Guard writes against the running plan's declared files_modified, at the moment of the write. workflow.blast_radius asks the same question at verify:pre, after the edits are on disk and usually committed — the answer there is a revert, here it is 'not that file'. "ask" escalates to the user (the model cannot self-approve); "deny" blocks outright, for unattended runs where there is nobody to ask. Writes under .planning/, paths covered by a declared glob or directory, and phases whose plans declare nothing are all allowed — the last of those is blast_radius's case, which refuses rather than passes. Implemented by hooks/gsd-prohibition-guard.js (PreToolUse).

workflow.test_tamper_guard.description: Guard existing test files against writes that remove assertions or newly skip tests. workflow.assertion_ratchet catches the same deletion at verify:pre against .planning/assertion-baseline.json; this catches it at the write, using the same notion of an assertion so the two cannot disagree. Creating a test file is always allowed, and adding assertions is never blocked. Implemented by hooks/gsd-test-tamper-guard.js (PreToolUse).

workflow.exit_gate.description: Command run when an executor subagent stops; a non-zero exit refuses the stop and hands the command's own output back for repair. Empty (the default) leaves the gate inert — only the project knows what green means for it. Typical values: "lefthook run pre-commit", "nx affected -t lint,typecheck --base=HEAD", "npm run lint:ci". Runs in the tree the subagent worked in (git rev-parse --show-toplevel from its cwd), never the main checkout — judging a worktree agent against somebody else's uncommitted WIP once reported 19 untouched files as its failure. Implemented by hooks/gsd-exit-gate.js (SubagentStop).

workflow.exit_gate_agents.description: Comma-separated subagent names that workflow.exit_gate applies to. Defaults to the executor alone; add others only if their output is the kind a lint/typecheck run can judge. A comma-separated string rather than a list because the capability config schema admits boolean, string, number and enum only.

workflow.exit_gate_max_retries.description: How many times workflow.exit_gate may refuse a stop for one phase-and-worktree before it reports instead of blocking. Past this, the failure travels to verification rather than looping an executor against debt it may not own. The check still RUNS after the budget is spent — a green tree clears the ledger and re-arms the gate; skipping the run would disarm it permanently for that worktree.

workflow.exit_gate_timeout.description: Seconds workflow.exit_gate may run before it is killed. A killed gate allows the stop — a gate that could not run is a configuration problem, not a code problem, and conflating the two trains people to disable it.

workflow.pin_invariants.description: Re-state the running plan's prohibitions and must-haves, plus any open blocker and the CLAUDE.md block between the gsd:pinned open and close comment markers, after a compaction rewrites them out of context. Measured effect of the omission: rule-violation rates go 0%→30-59% across models after compaction, and verbatim re-injection returns them to 0% (arXiv 2606.22528). Claude Code re-injects the project-root CLAUDE.md but neither path-scoped rules nor anything under .planning/. Implemented by hooks/gsd-pin-invariants.js on SessionStart: Claude Code re-fires it with source "compact" after a compaction, and the pin answers as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. PostCompact cannot add context, so the pin is not registered there.

workflow.pin_invariants_budget.description: Character cap on the workflow.pin_invariants injection. A pin that grows without bound recreates the problem it solves; over the cap, whole blocks are dropped at an item boundary and the omission is stated rather than hidden.

workflow.contract_drift.description: Block verify when a signature declared in DESIGN.md ## Contracts no longer matches the code. A phase declaring no signatures passes — the gate is silent where there is nothing to compare.

workflow.wave_collision.description: Block when two plans in the same wave declare the same file in files_modified. Same-wave plans run concurrently in separate worktrees, so a shared file means the second commit overwrites the first or conflicts. Measured at 13.4% of phases.

workflow.wave_normalize.description: Resolve directories and globs against the working tree before comparing same-wave files_modified (check mn-wave-collision in expand mode), and report a plan that declared nothing, a glob that matched nothing, and a prose entry under separate headings. Also switches check mn-wave-solve to the resolved file sets. Supersedes workflow.wave_collision for projects whose plans declare directories: literal comparison sees only entries with a dot in the basename, which skipped entries on 17 of 55 measured phases and reported a real wave-1 collision on a 40-file directory as clean. Enabling it alone also turns the gate on; with both keys on, the expand mode applies. Default false: resolution is against the tree, so a phase whose files do not exist yet will legitimately report RESOLVED TO NOTHING.

workflow.orphan_plans.description: Block verify when a plan declares status: in_progress but produced no SUMMARY — the executor started and never finished, so the next pass re-runs it on top of its own unrecorded work. Plans with no status at all are reported, not blocked: 37.4% of live plans are in that state and a gate failing a third of the repository gets switched off.

workflow.wave_solve.description: Block at plan:post when a declared wave breaks the parallelism invariant — a plan declared at or before the wave of a plan it depends on (it would run before its dependency exists), or sharing a declared wave and a file with another plan (it races it). The computed assignment (depends_on levels, then file-overlap stages) is reported for renumbering; a wave declared LATER than computed is reported, not blocked: sequential where parallel would do, slower but never wrong. A dependency cycle cannot be checked and blocks.

workflow.plan_status_enforce.description: Block at execute:wave:post when a plan's declared status contradicts what is on disk: an in_progress plan that produced no SUMMARY (the executor started and never finished, so the next pass re-runs it over its own uncommitted work), a status outside the vocabulary in_progress|blocked|done|superseded, a blocked plan with no blocked_reason, a superseded plan naming no successor, or a blocked_reason past 2048 characters. What it deliberately does NOT block: a plan carrying no status at all passes — 37.4% of live plans are in that state and a gate that fails a third of a repository is switched off permanently rather than fixed; and a correctly-declared blocked plan passes, because declaring a blockage is the behaviour the gate exists to reward, not to punish. Default false inverts GSD's usual absent-means-enabled on purpose: an enforcement gate that armed itself on upgrade would fail trees that never opted in.

workflow.refute_findings.description: Put the plan-checker's findings through an adversarial pass before the planner sees them: gsd-finding-refuter must try to disprove each one, and may only drop a finding with evidence — a file, a line, or a command's output. A reviewer whose findings are never challenged drifts toward reporting more of them, because an unreported real issue is visibly a miss while a reported non-issue costs it nothing; the cost lands on the planner rewriting plans to satisfy findings that were never true. Self-critique by the reviewer is the wrong shape and measurably worse (recall 27%->33%, signal-to-noise 5.11->1.95, arXiv 2603.11078) — the pass has to come from something that is not the reviewer. Deliberately one refuter and not a panel: five critics per plan is the ceremony the workflows guidance warns against. Expect it to change nothing most of the time; a refuter that regularly refutes half the findings is disputing on argument rather than evidence, which its evidence lines will show.

workflow.type_model.description: Instruct the planner to fix the phase's type model — domain vocabulary and branded ids, the closed error-code set, port signatures with their full return types, which Zod schema is authoritative, and any domain state the type cannot hold — BEFORE the tasks that write behaviour. In this codebase the type is the specification (2,646 files import @monads, 1,696 use Zod, 289 *.error-code.ts, and ~60 oxc rules enforce the shape), yet nothing in the pipeline asked for those decisions: the lint layer enforces the SHAPE of a decision and fires only once code exists, by which point whoever typed first made it. An empty section is a legitimate answer for a phase that introduces no types; an absent one is not. Port signatures land under DESIGN.md ## Contracts, where workflow.contract_drift already reads them.

workflow.enforcement_provenance.description: Require every review finding to name what guards it — a rule and where it runs, or "review only". A check is a mechanism only once it has an assigned execution point: a script nothing invokes is worse than none, because it creates the impression the invariant is guarded and removes the question from review while checking nothing. "This is a violation" and "CI will catch this" are separate claims and the second is wrong more often than expected — several boundary rules that read as general are hardcoded to one domain, and a rule at warn in a project that tolerates warnings guards nothing. The distinction changes the fix: a review-only finding recurs the moment nobody looks, so it ships with a mechanism or is knowingly accepted. Taken from the doctrine in the author's own mn/docs/architecture/enforcement.md, where it is a mandatory review step.

workflow.failure_paths.description: Instruct the planner to write the pre-mortem into PLAN.md as <failure_paths>: each <failure_path> names an <invariant> and a <check> — the <automated>/<fails_when> pair of #3172, judged by the same recognizer as the failing-direction probe — that fails when the invariant breaks. Required only of a plan whose files_modified names a migration or whose user_setup is non-empty; every other plan pays nothing. The planner self-checks with gsd_run check mn-failure-paths before returning; the verdict reports paths_without_check / paths — the share of named failures nothing would notice. Never halts; workflow.failure_paths_enforce does. On by default (absent = enabled): it adds an instruction to the planner's prompt and blocks nothing.

workflow.failure_paths_enforce.description: Halt plan:post when the failure-paths verdict has a blocker: a required plan with no <failure_path>, a path with no <check> command, a check whose <fails_when> is missing, empty or a placeholder, or an empty or placeholder <invariant>. An unreadable plan also halts — could not look is not clean. Default false: halting at plan:post has no revision loop behind it, so a project opts in once its plans carry the block. Assumes workflow.failure_paths is on; with it off the planner is not asked for the block the gate demands.

workflow.restate_goal.description: Instruct the planner to restate the phase goal in its own words before decomposing, as three lines at the end of every <objective>: Restated (the goal, not copied, and this plan's part), Not doing (what the phase leaves out, with sources) and Sources (ROADMAP goal, success criteria, CONTEXT D-NN, SPEC AC-n). A wrong reading of the goal is cheapest to catch before code exists; the plan-checker compares the lines with the goal (Dimension 1b) and treats a contradiction, or an exclusion a requirement needs, as a blocker. Extends the existing <objective> rather than adding a field. On by default (absent = enabled): an instruction, no gate.
